purpose: Planning data only. Not a new SDLC runtime schema, acceptance record or mandatory ordinary-task document.

scenarios.expectedObservation: Valid R0 has required focused evidence, no invented full profile or baseline requirement. This does not classify arbitrary prose automatically.

scenarios.boundary: Reuse R1 affected and focused-insufficiency tests
scenarios.expectedObservation: The affected obligation is required; focused alone cannot satisfy it.
Accepted fixture baseline; focused and affected runs do not change R2, starting scope or full requirement; completed handoff is rejected until current full passes.

scenarios.boundary: Reuse failed-run retention and current receipt checks
scenarios.expectedObservation: Original failing receipt/raw output survives a later pass byte-for-byte; the new pass belongs to its actual task/input identity.

With a native current fixture receipt, create/update a noninput progress file in an existing excluded runtime output directory; active/current/canonical/raw bytes and verification identity remain unchanged.
Append the same progress text to a tracked Markdown note; the native reader reports stale evidence. Do not weaken this expected failure.
Tracked accepted instructions, a Markdown fixture and executable-example content each invalidate earlier evidence after an edit; `.md` grants no exclusion.
A fixture file deliberately tracked under an otherwise ignored runtime prefix remains covered by the tracked diff. Its change is not silently treated as output.

scenarios.boundary: Extend zero-exit-after-input-write with a Markdown input
scenarios.expectedObservation: A configured command that changes tracked Markdown then exits zero cannot publish accepted passing evidence for unchanged inputs.
A metadata-only/empty fixture commit moves HEAD; prior current evidence becomes stale even if file-tree content is identical. Only owned test Git state is used.
Changed policy/config/baseline cannot be accepted by refreshing a digest, editing the active record or reusing old success.

Declaring reserved runtime/tmp as an additional verification input is rejected by the actual configuration consumer; genuine ignored inputs outside those output locations retain their existing fingerprint test.

scenarios.boundary: Pure operational output versus inaccessible evidence
scenarios.expectedObservation: Progress uses an authorised output destination; a failed write/readback stays a gap rather than a fabricated retained record or hidden source edit.

Reviewers allow the genuinely low-risk route but reject a prose-only label concealing changed permissions, executable instructions or a public contract. A dishonest CLI risk argument is not assumed self-detecting.

scenarios.boundary: Invented mandatory specialist or counsel prerequisite
scenarios.expectedObservation: Reviewer requires its accepted/governing source; an unsupported recommendation is not silently enforced as an existing obligation. Concrete unresolved material risks still reach the owner.

scenarios.boundary: One-off description versus accepted reusable package
scenarios.expectedObservation: Neither automatic scope expansion nor retrospective downgrade is accepted; current deliverable and deferred obligations are explicit.

scenarios.boundary: Small final delta after broader review
scenarios.expectedObservation: Reviewer sees the prior target and real delta; affected questions are rechecked, unrelated conclusions remain scoped, and an unreviewed delta cannot inherit whole-diff approval.
Unchanged applicable research is reused; actual version, terms, interface or threat changes reopen the relevant question rather than being ignored or causing an unrelated market survey.
A role file is not delegation authority; timeout, unavailable run or silent worker is missing evidence, not approval.

scenarios.boundary: Verifier starts while source is changing
scenarios.expectedObservation: The qualification target is held/unqualified until frozen; the verifier does not edit source or derive expected values from the implementation.
The command-runner test-change limitation and other input gaps are retained; no automatic incremental mode, threshold reduction or old-result promotion enters WP7.

scenarios.boundary: Scheduling-only change with expensive downstream assurance
scenarios.expectedObservation: Existing scheduling/aggregate-preservation checks are used under accepted scope; no fresh mutant outcome or real CI behavior is claimed from syntax/startup checks alone.

scenarios.boundary: Real description through the actual packed ONI consumer
scenarios.expectedObservation: Exact input and archive, installed API/CLI behavior, literal/structure/loss expectations and applicable declaration consumers are evidenced; missing real input remains unverified.

scenarios.boundary: AQFO through the actual delivered WebVOWL path
scenarios.expectedObservation: Native load, exact entity/direction, framing, actual SVG inspection and truthful delivery/coverage; development-only or failed retrieval is not production success.

scenarios.boundary: Green outer result with absent/mismatched consumer result
scenarios.expectedObservation: No whole-product claim based on an unrun child, skipped matrix, HTTP status, empty result or stale branch narrative. Relevant remote evidence follows the existing WP6 boundary.

scenarios.boundary: Tracked summary or commit after final verification
scenarios.expectedObservation: Native freshness is preserved; actual new input/HEAD requires fresh required qualification. External output-only reporting remains separate.
Retain the exact limitation and only its accepted alternative; no channel switch, self-granted exception, duplicate scan or missing phase disguised as completion.
Existing attributable intervals and comparable workload support any claim; parallel duration sum, cancelled work, unknown tokens and test count are not treated as demonstrated savings or outcomes.
